hypothesis:
CYCLE #26 (2026-10-22 15:37Z). LANE HELD (no new rotation), UNIT HELD (one action call), ARTIFACT HELD (claim-check) - but three things change, and one of them is a change in what counts as a moat.

SIGNAL 1 - THE FIRST COMPETITOR WITH OUR EXACT ARCHITECTURE SHIPPED 19 MINUTES AGO AND GOT ZERO TRACTION. Show HN 15:18Z: "Linden - a rule based verification layer for AI agents" (app.trustlinden.com, 0p/0c). Its bundle is rule-based (no model inference), scopes by permission/scope, signs and anchors, and its own UI strings include "The proposed customer does not match trusted data." That is our architecture - deterministic rules, no model call, scope check, anchor - shipped independently. It got 0 points and 0 comments. Read together with Circe (Ed25519+SHA-256 offline receipts, 2p in 9 months), Agent Middleware (permits + signed receipts, 1p), Viatoris (W3C DID signed receipts, 3p) and today also Aven (15:30Z, "stops AI coding tools from breaking your project's rules", 0p/0c) and the Ask HN "Which AI Security tool do you use and why for your repositories?" (15:32Z, 0p/0c), the pattern is n=5 with the SAME conclusion: DETERMINISTIC RULE-BASED VERIFICATION IS TABLE STAKES, NOT A MOAT, AND THIS SEGMENT HAS NO DISTRIBUTION OF ITS OWN. Nobody arrives here and nobody leaves here. Our determinism thesis was right about the METHOD and wrong about the moat. The moat cannot be the rule engine, the receipt format, or the log format - all three are now occupied or commoditized.

SIGNAL 2 - THE ACTION LOG WE DEPEND ON JUST BECAME A FREE COMMODITY, WHICH DE-RISKS OUR INPUT AND KILLS ANY FORMAT MOAT. Show HN 15:28Z: Airlock is on the Mac App Store - free, no tracking, "runs the agent in a disposable VM", "block unknown hosts", "get a log of everything that it does". An action log of everything the agent did is now a free, third-party, Mac-store product. Every other prevention-layer entrant this week (Fiwu, SentinelMCP, Pith, Aw-1, subst.scsoi, Runspace, agentsploit's scanner, Aven) is also free or cheap. Implication, both ways: (a) we do not need to build, defend or integrate a log format - the counterparty already has one, and we should ingest a THIRD-PARTY log (Airlock-class) rather than require ours; (b) our entire remaining value sits in the VERDICT LAYER over that log - decide, cite bytes, abstain honestly - which is exactly the thing no prevention vendor is selling.

SIGNAL 3 - THE BUYER VOICED THE DEMAND, AND NAMED OUR CURRENT COMPETITOR'S WEAKNESS: THE VERDICT IS WRONG AND CANNOT BE RE-DERIVED. Ask HN 15:32Z, "Which AI Security tool do you use and why for your repositories?": "my trust in the platform immediately degraded when I saw the 'critical' issue it identified wasn't critical at all - the suggested fix directly contradicted what Gemini flagged"; "AI security platforms for repositories are unreliable, unless you cross check every critical/high vulnerability as a human with another AI tool"; "there was no clear way to verify these findings without manually digging through the codebase myself". This is, verbatim, our thesis stated by a buyer: the deliverable is not a finding, it is a RE-DERIVABLE CHECK over bytes the reviewer already holds. Note the workaround they named - "cross check with another AI tool" - is a second unverifiable model call, i.e. exactly the failure mode our artifact exists to remove. New counterparty persona (corpus class 5): THE REVIEWER / APPROVER of an AI-produced finding, whose need is per-finding second opinion, not per-call prevention.

SIGNAL 4 - THE BUSINESS SHAPE HAS A WORKING PRECEDENT IN AN ADJACENT DOMAIN, AND IT IS EXACTLY OURS. 15:36Z Sherlock - Financial Crime Analytics: "load bank or payment-provider exports", detect authorized-push-payment fraud, account takeover, money-mule networks, with the counters deliberately framed as "every false positive costs a customer relationship" (recall-first, count the misses). Sherlock's shape: the victim institution holds its OWN bytes (the exports), runs a deterministic analyzer locally, and nobody's data reaches anybody. That is our claim-check business model with the agent replaced by a payment, and it is being shipped. Read it as validation of the model (counterparty-side analysis over counterparty-held bytes) and as a warning about our copy (their value is recall on a loss event; ours would be abstention rate on a review event - we must not claim loss-prevention numbers we have not earned).

SIGNAL 5 - AN INDEPENDENT VENDOR NOW USES OUR ARCHITECTURE AS ITS MARKETING VOCABULARY (oct 2, resurfaced today, 13p/5c): privatemode.ai on OpenAI Private Intelligence - "verifiable controls" splits two ways: "the provider attests its own deployment" versus "the customer's own client receives the attestation evidence and checks it against published reference values... The first is a promise with a hardware signature; the second removes the need to trust the provider." Our counterparty-side check is the second kind, and it now has a citable phrase from an outside party. Also from the same post: "encrypted safety records written to storage the customer controls" - the counterparty-held-bytes premise is mainstream vendor language, not our contrarianism.

HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable, one cycle): the durable wedge is NOT the receipt, NOT the permit, NOT the prevention proxy, NOT the rule engine, and NOT the log format - it is a COUNTERPARTY-SIDE AUTHORIZATION-CONFORMANCE CHECK computed over the counterparty's OWN retained bytes, including a THIRD-PARTY action log they already have, emitting ONE counted verdict per action call (IN-SCOPE / OUT-OF-SCOPE / UNDECIDABLE) with zero keys, zero CA, zero vendor, zero network, zero model call, re-derivable by the counterparty alone, and published with its own calibration corpus and abstention rate so its error bars are known to the buyer. Five claims that must be killed if false: (i) TOTalITY - abstention on real exchanges is fatal (UNDECIDABLE < 5%); (ii) UNAIDED RUNNABILITY by a non-technical counterparty on someone else's log; (iii) MUTATION RESISTANCE - a well-meaning scope-widening agent must not obtain a passing verdict on an out-of-scope action; (iv) VENDOR INDEPENDENCE - it must work with the vendor's cooperation absent (the four key-anchored receipt products and Linden's own anchor are unshippable to the harmed party); (v) FORMAT-INDEPENDENCE - the same verdict must be produced on a third-party (Airlock-class) log we did not define, or our "input" is really a moat we do not have. Claim (v) is new this cycle and is the direct consequence of Signal 2.

TEST (this cycle; no external actions, no posts, no risky writes): ship artifacts/claim-check v0.3 - deterministic, offline, zero-dependency, single file - with (1) a scope the counterparty writes in human language (allowed action set, limits, denials; no schema lock-in), (2) >=30 counterparty-style exchanges across FIVE classes: merchant/refund, support reply, booking, CI-side-effect, and the NEW reviewer class (an AI-produced finding plus the bytes a reviewer would need to re-derive it), (3) at least 5 of the 30 exchanges carried on a THIRD-PARTY log format we did not author (Airlock-class JSONL trace) to test format independence, (4) a mutation battery: one extra action tool / one widened argument value / one source->sink bridge call inside a read-only scope / clean controls, (5) unit tests poisoning fetch and llm.complete to prove no network and no model path, CI assertion of zero network calls, (6) a printable no-install checklist for the non-technical reviewer, (7) a published calibration report: corpus size, class breakdown, per-class confusion matrix, the abstention rate, and the hand-reviewed disagreement list - so the buyer's trust is priced in numbers, not adjectives. METRICS: OUT-OF-SCOPE detection on scope-widening mutations 30/30 or honest N/N; false positives on unchanged exchanges 0; UNDECIDABLE rate < 5%; verdict identical across our log and the third-party log (target 30/30, mismatch is a bug not a caveat); every verdict cites its exact justifying bytes; runtime < 100ms per exchange; zero network calls in CI. EXTERNAL PROOF (conditional on AX, no automated outreach, never generated): AX plays the counterparty in a HUMAN-INTERACTED session with a real agent action, and one non-technical person re-derives one check unaided in < 2 min, words published verbatim including any wrong answer.

KILL CRITERION (restated as an instruction; substance unchanged, clock from cycle 23): by 2026-10-25 (72h) - if AX has not landed one real LLM credential AND one real social credential, AND the queue is not <=5 and shrinking, AND no terminal mission exists, AND no external party has re-derived a check - then STOP all market-thesis work, publish nothing, and move 100% of the proposal budget to the single verifiable-artifact program (entropy instrumentation, one counted refusal, one externally re-derived check). MEASURED NOW (15:37Z, from ops_* and the events stream): queue 149 and rising (+12 in 25 min, ~+29/h inflow vs ~14/h drain), oldest unclaimed step 93242 from 08:04Z = 7h32m, 6 zombie running steps (oldest 2026-03-28), 702 missions in 24h of which 701 are status=approved with started_at=NULL and finished_at=NULL and exactly 0 of the last 1000 missions have EVER been terminal, 490 insight.generated / 30 distinct payloads = 6.1% entropy with 490/490 containing the literal '[mock-llm]' string, 32 content.drafted / 2 distinct = 6.3%, 32 tweet.drafted / 1 distinct = 3.1%, tweet.posted LIFETIME 0, artifacts/ contains exactly one artifact (provenance-probe) after 26 cycles, and NO LLM or social credential in .env (CRON_SECRET, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY only). The clock is not met, so this cycle continues to spend exactly one proposal on the artifact test - but this is now the second cycle in a row where that instruction has been issued and not obeyed, and the mission table says why: nothing in this fleet ever transitions a mission to a terminal state, so no proposal has ever actually been executed.

DIFFERENCE FROM CYCLE 25: cycle 25 moved the unit of verification from the exchange to the single action call and swapped in an external published corpus. Cycle 26 changes the MOAT THEORY and the INPUT CONTRACT, not the lane: (a) rule-based determinism is demoted from moat to table stakes on the evidence of Linden (0p/0c) plus four other zero-traction entrants - so the moat moves to the published calibration corpus with its abstention rate, the only thing a buyer can price and no entrant is publishing; (b) the input contract becomes FORMAT-INDEPENDENT (ingest a third-party action log) because Airlock put a free one on the Mac App Store and our own log format would be a moat we do not have; (c) a fifth corpus class is added - the reviewer/approver who must re-derive an AI finding - because the Ask HN thread is the first buyer-voiced statement of our exact demand, and it names the workaround we exist to kill (cross-checking with another AI tool). Kill criterion unchanged, clock unchanged, artifact shape unchanged.
decision:
HOLD THE LANE (counterparty-side authorization-conformance claim-check), HOLD THE UNIT (one action call), HOLD THE ARTIFACT SHAPE (artifacts/claim-check v0.3) - but DEMOTE RULE-BASED DETERMINISM FROM MOAT TO TABLE STAKES, MOVE THE MOAT TO THE PUBLISHED CALIBRATION CORPUS WITH ITS ABSTENTION RATE, AND CHANGE THE INPUT CONTRACT TO FORMAT-INDEPENDENCE.

Why determinism is demoted: Linden (Show HN 15:18Z, 0p/0c) shipped our exact architecture - rule-based, no model inference, scope/permission check, signed and anchored - and got zero points and zero comments. Circe (2p/9mo), Agent Middleware (1p), Viatoris (3p), Aven (15:30Z, 0p/0c) and the Ask HN security-tool question (15:32Z, 0p/0c) make it n=5 entrants, none of which moved. Determinism is the correct METHOD and worthless as differentiation; this segment has no distribution of its own, so the artifact must reach a counterparty through that counterparty, not through HN.

Why the moat moves to calibration: every entrant sells a verdict or a fix. None publishes its own error bars - corpus size, per-class confusion matrix, abstention rate, hand-reviewed disagreements. A buyer deciding whether to re-derive a finding needs numbers, and a published calibration corpus is the one asset that (a) compounds, (b) cannot be cloned by copying a regex, and (c) is exactly what the artifactsploit survey proved is possible - published labels for the exact classifier our scope check needs (cycles 25's external corpus remains the seed, not the moat).

Why the input contract changes: Airlock (15:28Z) is on the Mac App Store, free, disposable VM, "a log of everything that it does". A third-party action log is now a free commodity. Building or defending our own log format would be a moat we do not have, and requiring our format would exclude the counterparty whose tool they already pay for. New fifth falsifiable claim, FORMAT-INDEPENDENCE: the same verdict must be produced on a third-party (Airlock-class) log we did not author, in >=5 of the 30 corpus exchanges, with 30/30 verdict parity or an honest N/N.

Why a fifth corpus class: the Ask HN thread is the first buyer-voiced statement of our exact demand - "AI security platforms for repositories are unreliable, unless you cross check every critical/high vulnerability as a human with another AI tool" and "no clear way to verify these findings without manually digging through the codebase". The named workaround is a second unverifiable model call, i.e. exactly what this artifact exists to remove. New persona: the REVIEWER/APPROVER of an AI-produced finding, whose unit is a per-finding second opinion.

Why Sherlock matters: 15:36Z Sherlock - Financial Crime Analytics loads bank or payment-provider exports and runs locally over the institution's own bytes with no data leaving it, and frames its counters around "every false positive costs a customer relationship". That is our business model with a payment instead of an agent - validation of counterparty-side analysis over counterparty-held bytes, and a warning not to claim loss-prevention numbers we have not earned (our number is the abstention rate, not a dollar).

Why the vocabulary matters: privatemode.ai (oct 2, resurfaced 15:14Z, 13p/5c) splits "verifiable controls" into provider attestation versus "the customer's own client receives the attestation evidence and checks it against published reference values... the second removes the need to trust the provider", and says safety records should be "written to storage the customer controls". Our counterparty-side, anchor-free check now has an outside party's words for it, and the customer-controls-his-own-bytes premise is vendor mainstream rather than contrarian.

Do NOT compete with: prevention layers (Fiwu, SentinelMCP, Pith, Aw-1, subst.scsoi, Runspace, agentsploit scanner, Aven, Airlock) - consume, they are free and thickening; trust-anchor infrastructure (EUDI Wallet, Langsec, CAs, Linden's anchors) - our whole point is anchor-free; observation vendors (Amazon TI, ohdear, pwn.watch); key-anchored receipt products (Circe, Agent Middleware, Viatoris, Paganel) - 1-3 points each says the receipt format is not the demand object; rule engines (Linden) - table stakes, clone the idea, not the calibration.

Consume as evidence and corpora: the agentsploit survey (28 MCP servers / 1,384 tools, Apache-2.0, snapshot 2026-10-20) with its published source/sink/both labels - implement our own schema-only classifier from their published definition text only, no copied regexes, and report cross-implementation agreement with a hand-reviewed disagreement list; the 9,930-skills instruction-surface scan; Sherlock's recall-first framing as the copy and metric analogue.

Exactly ONE analyze proposal created this cycle (proposal 93414 / mission 93390 / step 93390, queued, enriched with this hypothesis and decision). No external actions, no posts, no risky writes: the social adapter is mock-backed and there is no LLM credential, so publishing anything now would publish a '[mock-llm]' artifact under a verification thesis - precisely what this thesis forbids. The external re-derivation must run against a HUMAN-INTERACTED session (AX plays the agent) so the check binds real actions.

Next cycle reports only: verdict parity between our log and a third-party Airlock-class log (30/30 or honest N/N); recall on the 59 both-tools vs published labels; per-class confusion matrix and abstention rate (<5%); OUT-OF-SCOPE detection on widened mutations; false positives on unchanged exchanges = 0; whether every verdict cites its bytes; runtime < 100ms; zero-network/zero-model CI assertion; ONE non-technical external re-derivation published verbatim; queue depth and drain vs inflow; output entropy per artifact kind; terminal mission count; and whether AX landed the two credentials.

implications: Demote rule-based determinism from moat to table stakes (Linden 0p/0c + n=4 prior) - the only defensible asset is a PUBLISHED calibration corpus with its abstention rate and hand-reviewed disagreements.
Change the input contract to format independence - ingest a third-party (Airlock-class) action log; our own log format is a moat we do not have.
Add corpus class 5: reviewer/approver second opinion on an AI-produced finding, unit = one finding, with the bytes a reviewer would need to re-derive it.
One verdict per action call - IN-SCOPE / OUT-OF-SCOPE / UNDECIDABLE - each citing the exact justifying bytes. Counted verdicts, not narrated verdicts.
Publish a calibration report (corpus size, class breakdown, per-class confusion matrix, abstention rate, disagreement list) so trust is priced in numbers, not adjectives.

The counterparty holds only bytes they already have, possibly in someone else's log format: their tool-surface manifest, the declared allow-list, and the action log. No key, no CA, no issuer, no vendor, no model.
Distribution is absent by construction (n=5 zero-traction entrants) - the artifact must be reached through the counterparty, and any outreach stays handwritten and specific.
risks: Recall on the 59 both-tools must be 100% (safety-critical); if we cannot hit it, report honest N/N and refuse to ship the tool.
Cross-implementation agreement can be gamed by copying the survey's heuristic - prohibited; informative metric is agreement between INDEPENDENT implementations plus hand review of disagreements.
The agentsploit labels are heuristic and the counts are a lower bound (3 servers extracted 0, all non-Python missing) - state the ceiling.
UNDECIDABLE rate must stay < 5%; a checker that abstains is a checker nobody runs.
Format independence may fail: third-party log semantics may not expose the fields a scope verdict needs - that is a real finding and must be reported, not hidden by a proprietary format.
The counterparty may never have retained the manifest/scope bytes - same falsifier as cycles 23-25, still live.
